options: A key that only works for exactly 24 hours before being permanently deleted
A key that customers are required to type in manually every time data is read
A key that must be physically mailed to the customer before use
A key the cloud provider generates and fully manages for you automatically, with zero setup required
questions.explain: Platform-managed keys are generated and managed entirely by the provider, which is why default encryption needs no configuration.

questions.q: What extra control does a customer-managed key (CMK) actually give you, compared to a platform-managed key?
options: Control over the rotation schedule, a detailed audit log of every use, and the ability to revoke or delete the key yourself
The ability to skip encryption entirely for a lower cost
Automatic compliance certification with no further action needed
Faster encryption performance than AES-256
questions.explain: CMKs are generated and controlled by the customer in Key Vault or KMS, giving real control over rotation, auditing, and revocation.

questions.q: Why do some compliance frameworks require customer-managed keys even though both key types use the same AES-256 encryption?
options: Compliance frameworks have no actual opinion on key management
Platform-managed keys are not actually encrypted at all
Customer-managed keys use a stronger, different encryption algorithm than platform-managed keys
Auditors want documented proof that the customer, not the vendor, controls access to the data
questions.explain: The cryptography is the same either way — the compliance value of a CMK is demonstrable customer control over key access.

questions.q: What real risk does a customer-managed key introduce that a platform-managed key does not?
options: If you delete or lose access to the CMK, the data it protected becomes permanently, cryptographically unreadable, with no recovery path
Customer-managed keys expire after exactly one use
There is no additional risk; CMKs are strictly safer in every respect
A customer-managed key automatically shares your data with the cloud provider
questions.explain: Losing a CMK permanently locks you out of the data it protected, since the entire point is that nobody, including the provider, can bypass it.

options: Deliberately deleting a customer-managed key to instantly and irreversibly destroy access to everything it protects
An automated process that rotates platform-managed keys every hour
A type of encryption algorithm used only for shredded documents
A method for physically destroying a hard drive with a paper shredder
questions.explain: Crypto-shredding uses the irrecoverable nature of a deleted key as a deliberate, instant way to destroy access to protected data.
